purpose: Alpelisib is used to treat certain types of breast cancer in adults, specifically hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer that has a PIK3CA gene mutation and has spread to other parts of the body. It is also used to treat a rare condition called PROS (PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum) in adults and children. It is usually given along with another hormone-blocking medicine called fulvestrant for breast cancer.
how_it_works: Cancer cells sometimes have a faulty gene called PIK3CA that sends signals telling them to grow out of control. Alpelisib works by blocking a protein called PI3K that this faulty gene activates, which helps slow down or stop the cancer cells from growing and dividing. Think of it like putting a roadblock on the pathway the cancer cells use to grow.
common_side_effects: High blood sugar (very common — you may feel extra thirsty, tired, or need to urinate more), diarrhea, nausea, mouth sores, rash, decreased appetite, weight loss, low red blood cell count, and feeling tired. Your doctor will monitor your blood sugar closely.
warnings: This medication can cause serious high blood sugar (hyperglycemia), which can be life-threatening — tell your doctor right away if you feel very thirsty, confused, or urinate a lot. It can also cause severe skin rashes, serious diarrhea, and lung problems. If you have diabetes or pre-diabetes, your doctor needs to know before you start. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant, as it can harm the baby. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, as some can interact with alpelisib.
typical_dosing: For breast cancer, the usual dose is 300 mg (three 100 mg tablets) taken by mouth once a day with food. For PROS, the dose is lower and based on body weight. Always take it at the same time each day with a meal to help reduce stomach upset, and swallow the tablets whole — do not crush or chew them.
